claims.statement: All backend HTTP routers are mounted under a single `APIRouter(prefix="/api/v1")` in `src/main.py` (account, portfolio, auth, institutions, integration, market), while the WebSocket and worker-dashboard routers are mounted outside that prefix; the frontend `apiClient` hard-codes the same `/api/v1` base.

Editing a backend model requires a matching Alembic revision shipped in the same change, and every migration file MUST follow the `<hash>_<description>.py` naming convention under `migrations/versions/` (`alembic.ini` sets `script_location = migrations`); manual SQL migrations are created via autogenerate and use `op.execute()` inside a standard revision, and `src/main.py` upgrades the database to `head` at startup except when `settings.environment == "test"`.

The `AccountModel` table `accounts` is unique on `(user_id, institution_id, external_id)`, carries `api_sync_enabled`, `net_deposits`, `last_sync_at` and a nullable `integration_user_id` foreign key to `integration_users.id`, and cascades `all, delete-orphan` to its positions and portfolio associations.

`InstitutionModel.csv_format` is a comma-separated positional template string using standardized `{placeholder}` tokens that maps each column of a broker CSV export in order; `csv_import_enabled` plus a non-null `csv_format` is the gate that enables CSV import for an institution, and `src/commands/seed.py` documents the worked Wealthsimple example.

`GenericCsvParser` is template-driven: it normalizes template and header tokens to lowercase snake_case, validates header count and per-column matches against alias sets (raising a specific `CsvParserError` subclass on mismatch), drops cash rows (`sec-c-*`, blank/`cash` symbol, `security_type == "cash"`) and option rows (OCC-style symbols, `option`/`derivative` types), and computes `average_cost` as `book_value / quantity` quantized to 4 decimals.

`PositionRepository.sync_by_account` implements position sync as a full replace: it deletes every `PositionModel` row for the account and re-inserts the supplied positions, so partial syncs cannot leave stale holdings.

`PositionService.sync_account_positions` is a no-op when the account has no `integration_user_id`, raises `ApiSyncDisabledError` when `api_sync_enabled` is false, and otherwise enqueues the broker sync via `IntegrationAccountApi`; `POST /accounts/{account_id}/sync` pre-checks the same flag and is rate-limited to 3 requests per minute.

Account holdings and totals convert every position value from the security/position currency into the account currency with `currency_converter.CurrencyConverter` and `stockholm.Money`, deriving `total_profit_loss` as `total_value - net_deposits` and reporting `total_profit_loss_percent` only when `net_deposits` is set and non-zero.

The account router exposes user chart preferences at `GET|PUT|PATCH /accounts/me/preferences`, backed by `UserApi.get_preferences`/`save_preferences`/`patch_preferences` on the `auth_users.preferences` JSON column; `model_dump(exclude_none=True)` drops explicit null fields so a PUT does not clear other keys.

`POST /accounts/csv/inspect`, `POST /accounts/csv/import`, and `POST /accounts/{account_id}/csv-sync` accept `institution_id`/`account_numbers`/`currencies` either as multipart form fields or as query parameters with the same alias; account numbers may be a JSON list string, a comma-separated string, or repeated values (normalized and deduplicated in order), and missing `institution_id` or `account_numbers` yields HTTP 422.

`CsvAccountService.inspect_csv` marks discovered accounts the user already has for that institution (`exists = True` and the stored currency), and `import_accounts` creates new accounts with `api_sync_enabled=False` or refreshes existing ones by re-syncing their positions, resolving each holding through `SecurityApi.get_or_create_from_broker` and wrapping resolution failures in `SecurityResolutionError`.

The auth domain persists five tables — `auth_users` (unique indexed email, argon2 `_password_hash`, `is_active`, `is_verified`, `last_login_at`, JSON `preferences`), `auth_verification_tokens`, `auth_totp`, `auth_recovery_codes`, and `auth_passkeys` — and the TOTP, recovery-code, and passkey tables cascade on user deletion.

`UserApi.login` returns a `LoginChallengeResponse` carrying a 5-minute `mfa_pending`-scope JWT instead of an access token when the user has a verified TOTP record; the client completes the challenge at `POST /auth/2fa/login-verify`, which sets the same `auth_token` cookie as password login.

`AuthorizationApi.check_entity_owned_by_user` raises HTTP 404 rather than 403 when the entity is missing or not owned by the user, deliberately hiding entity existence; `src/main.py` maps `AuthorizationError` and `EntityNotFoundError` to 404 responses with an `{"error": ...}` body.

`SecurityModel` is unique on `(symbol, exchange)` (allowing the same ticker on different venues) and `SecurityBrokerModel` records the broker to security mapping (institution, broker symbol/exchange, mapped symbol/exchange, `search_results` JSON) indexed on `(institution_id, broker_symbol, broker_exchange)`.

Price-related market tables are `market_prices` (unique `(security_id, date)`, OHLC plus `adjusted_close` as `DECIMAL(16,8)`) and `market_intraday_prices` (unique `(security_id, timestamp)`, 1-hour candles), and per-user market tables are keyed by `user_id` for watchlists, price alerts, security notes, security documents, and chart snapshots — with `market_chart_snapshots` indexed on `(security_id, user_id, captured_at)`.

`SecurityApi.get_or_create_from_broker` first checks the broker mapping table, then maps the broker symbol (`.` to `-`) and exchange (`CSE` to `CA`, `TSX` to `TO`, `NYSE` to `US`, `NASDAQ` to `US`), searches EODHD (through `SecuritySearchCache` when present), takes the first result, warms prices via `MarketPricesApi.get_latest_close`, and persists the mapping with the raw search results; zero search results raise `ValueError`.

`EodhdPriceRepository` is the registered `PriceRepository` implementation and adds read-through caching: `get_prices` merges stored rows with fresh EODHD rows (EODHD winning per date) and persists the union, `get_latest_price` only refetches when the stored close predates the last NYSE trading day (computed with `holidays.NYSE()`), and `save_price`/`save_prices` deliberately raise `NotImplementedError` so writes go through the inner SQLAlchemy repository.

`GET /market/prices/{security_id}` supports `interval` in `1d|1w|1m|1h|4h`: daily/weekly/monthly require both `from_date` and `to_date` (HTTP 422 otherwise) and aggregate in process, while intraday reads `market_intraday_prices` and lazily backfills via `MarketService.fetch_and_save_intraday_prices` when the stored window is stale.

The market router exposes price alerts, security notes, documents, and chart snapshots as per-security sub-resources under `/market/securities/{security_id}/...` (alerts GET/POST/DELETE, notes GET/POST/PUT/DELETE, documents GET/POST/DELETE, snapshots GET/POST 201/DELETE 204); note create and update both enqueue `generate_note_title_task` so the title is regenerated by AI in the worker, and document uploads are written to `settings.upload_path` under a random `uuid4` filename with only metadata persisted.

Indicator endpoints split between `GET /market/securities/{security_id}/indicators`, which computes MAs/MACD/RSI in process and caches results in Redis via `IndicatorCache`, and `POST .../indicators/compute`, which builds or accepts a candle series (aggregating weekly/monthly/4h as needed, optionally applying Heikin-Ashi) and delegates computation to the external Go sidecar through `IndicatorServiceClient`; caller-supplied candles bypass the cache.

The AI endpoints `POST /market/securities/{security_id}/ai/fundamentals`, `/ai/summarize-notes`, and `/ai/portfolio-debate` are each rate-limited to 5 requests per minute and map `TimeoutError` to HTTP 504 and `RuntimeError` to HTTP 503.

`MarketService` updates prices for all active securities — a one-year window daily and a seven-day window of 1-hour intraday candles hourly — pushing blocking gateway I/O through `asyncio.to_thread` and gathering per-security calls with `asyncio.gather`, swallowing per-security exceptions so one failure cannot abort the batch (returning `success`/`failure` counts).

`src/market/task.py` chains the scheduled pipeline: `daily_price_update` runs at midnight, `hourly_intraday_price_update` runs every hour and then enqueues `recalculate_all_account_totals_task` and `check_and_dispatch_price_alerts` in isolated try/except blocks, and the alert path ends in a retrying `alert_email_dispatch_task` that marks the alert triggered.

`IntegrationUserModel` (table `integration_users`) is unique on `(user_id, institution_id, external_user_id)`, and `IntegrationAccountApi.sync_account_positions` enqueues `sync_account_positions_task` with the broker gateway class resolved from the account's institution via `get_broker_gateway_class`.

`BrokerApiGateway` declares `login`, `get_accounts`, and `get_positions_by_account`, and its constructor unconditionally installs keyring's `PlaintextKeyring` — flagged with a TODO to secure before staging — so broker session tokens are stored in plaintext on disk.

`_sync_account_positions_task` orchestrates broker sync in the Huey worker: it marks the sync active in Redis, emits `ACCOUNT_SYNC_STARTED`, resolves each broker position to a security via `SecurityApi.get_or_create_from_broker`, replaces positions through `PositionApi.create`, refreshes `net_deposits`/`last_sync_at`, then emits success or a mapped plain-language error email plus `ACCOUNT_SYNC_FAILED`; the Redis marker is always cleared in `finally`, and an interrupted-task signal handler clears it for interrupted tasks.

The integration router exposes `GET /integration/institutions` for enabled institutions and `/external` endpoints for broker users, login (mapping `OTPRequiredError` to 400 `OTP_REQUIRED` and `LoginFailedError` to 401 `INVALID_CREDENTIALS`), account listing, `POST /external/accounts/import` (3/minute, deduplicating via `AccountApi.import_from_broker` and enqueuing one sync task per newly created account), and `POST /external/positions/import` for synchronous single-account import; every route touching an `IntegrationUser` first calls `check_entity_owned_by_user`.

`ConnectionManager` tracks per-user WebSocket connections and fans out messages by publishing a user_id and message payload to Redis Pub/Sub channel `ws_messages`, keeping one Redis client per running event loop and falling back to local delivery when publishing fails; `/api/ws` authenticates via a signed single-use ticket (verified with `max_age=30`, salt `ws-ticket`, replay-guarded by a Redis key with 30 s expiry) or the `auth_token` cookie / `sec-websocket-protocol` header, closing with 1008 on failure.

`src/core/exception.py` defines the two abstract base exceptions every domain error derives from — `EntityNotFoundError` (with `entity_id`/`entity_name`) and `AuthorizationError` (requiring `log_message()`) — and `src/main.py` maps both to HTTP 404 with an error body.

`src/core/pagination.py` defines `PaginationParams` (`offset >= 0`, `1 <= limit <= 100`, default 50) and the generic `PaginatedResponse` wrapper, which is the response shape used by account holdings, watchlist securities, alerts, and notes endpoints.

`register_services` in `src/config/services.py` binds `AsyncSession` to the session manager, registers core/account/auth services unconditionally, and then branches on `settings.stub_external_api` to register either live or stub integration and market services.

Each domain exposes its own `register_*_services(registry)` function (for example `register_account_services` and `register_market_services`) that registers repositories, APIs, and services as `svcs` factories, so nothing is constructed by hand in a handler.

Extending the backend requires: for a new domain, following the layered file set and calling `register_services` plus including the router in the `/api/v1` router in `src/main.py`; for a new broker, adding an `InstitutionEnum` value, seeding it, implementing `BrokerApiGateway`, and wiring `get_broker_gateway_class`; and for a new market provider, implementing `MarketGateway` and repointing the `MarketGateway` registration.

Tests must not depend on external services — Redis is globally faked, HTTP/broker/SMTP clients are stubbed or patched, and only the ephemeral testcontainers PostgreSQL is allowed — and the backend test suite is grouped into `tests/routers/`, `tests/services/`, per-domain folders such as `tests/account/` and `tests/market/`, `tests/integration/brokers/`, and `tests/ws/`.

The market router's watchlist surface (all routes gated on `current_user`) is `GET /market/watchlists`, `POST /market/watchlists` (201), `PATCH /market/watchlists/{watchlist_id}` (partial rename and/or `sort`, 409 on a duplicate name, and ownership is still proven for a no-op payload by raising `WatchlistNotFoundError` when the ID is not among the user's watchlists), `DELETE /market/watchlists/{watchlist_id}` (204), `GET /market/watchlists/{watchlist_id}/securities` (paginated `PaginatedResponse[SecuritySchema]`), `POST|DELETE /market/watchlists/{watchlist_id}/securities/{security_id}`, `PUT /market/watchlists/{watchlist_id}/securities/order` (422 on a non-permutation payload), and the default-watchlist shortcuts `POST|DELETE /market/watchlists/securities/{security_id}`; each membership mutation returns the updated `WatchlistRead` with its securities embedded.

`WatchlistRepository` (`src/market/repository.py`) is the contract the market router uses directly for watchlists — there is no watchlist service — and declares `get_by_user`, `create`, `rename`, `update_sort`, `set_security_order`, `delete`, `create_default`, the default-watchlist shortcuts `add_security`/`remove_security`, the per-watchlist `add_security_to_watchlist`/`remove_security_from_watchlist`, and the paged `get_securities`; the ABC requires every implementation to scope operations to the owning `user_id` and to report a watchlist that is missing *or* owned by another user as `WatchlistNotFoundError` so callers cannot distinguish the two, and documents that `set_security_order` accepts only an exact permutation of the current membership (including duplicates) and must leave positions unchanged otherwise.

`SqlAlchemyWatchlistRepository` converts the `(user_id, name)` unique violation into `WatchlistDuplicateNameError` after a rollback on both create and rename, resolves the default watchlist by the literal name `"Default"` (creating it on the first `add_security`, tolerating a concurrent-create `IntegrityError` by re-reading, and raising `WatchlistNotFoundError` from `remove_security` when absent), raises `SecurityNotFoundError` for an unknown security in membership edits, treats removing a non-member as a no-op, and price-enriches every returned `WatchlistRead`/`SecuritySchema` with `current_price`, `daily_price_change`, and `daily_price_change_percent` from one batched query over the latest two closes per security.

`WatchlistDuplicateNameError` deliberately extends plain `Exception` rather than `EntityNotFoundError`, so the global `EntityNotFoundError` handler does not turn it into a 404 and the watchlist routes translate it to HTTP 409.

Every market table that references a security holds a real foreign key to `market_securities.id` (`market_securities_broker`, `market_prices`, `market_intraday_prices`, `market_watchlists_securities`, `market_price_alerts`, `market_security_notes`, `market_security_documents`, `market_chart_snapshots`); the only cross-domain `security_id` column without a database-level foreign key is `account_positions.security_id` in the account domain.

The layering rules this page owns are: models generate migrations and are never returned to clients (routes return `*Read` schemas), repositories and services exchange schemas rather than ORM models, `api_types.py` is the only type surface that may cross a domain boundary, and a router may call its own domain's repositories directly for thin CRUD routes but must never touch a foreign domain's repositories.

Watchlist ordering and sort mode are persisted state: `market_watchlists.sort` stores a `WatchlistSortMode` (server default `custom`; also `name_asc`, `price_change_desc`, `price_change_asc`, `date_added`, `date_added_asc`) and `market_watchlists_securities.position` is an application-managed integer, backfilled deterministically by `security_id` ascending in migration `4c2ed77e7738_add_watchlist_sort_membership_added_at_.py`, which also adds and then makes NOT NULL the `added_at` association column. `WatchlistRead.securities` therefore holds `WatchlistSecuritySchema` entries carrying `added_at` and `position` in addition to the price fields, and the repository loads memberships by querying the association table directly because the `secondary` relationship cannot order by or carry those columns.

`SqlAlchemyWatchlistRepository.set_security_order` validates the payload against the current membership before writing anything: a length mismatch or set mismatch (which catches duplicates, missing IDs, and foreign IDs) raises `WatchlistOrderIdentityError`, otherwise it issues per-row `position` updates to `0..n-1` only when the order actually changed, so re-sending the current order is a no-op; membership adds append at `max(position) + 1`, which the implementation documents as not concurrency-safe, and `add_security_to_watchlist`/`remove_security_from_watchlist` explicitly reload the watchlist with `populate_existing=True` so the ORM collection reflects the explicit association INSERT/DELETE.

`WatchlistDuplicateNameError` and `WatchlistOrderIdentityError` are deliberately plain `Exception` subclasses rather than `EntityNotFoundError`s (`src/market/exception.py`), which is what lets the market router map a duplicate name to HTTP 409 and a non-permutation order payload to HTTP 422 instead of letting the global `EntityNotFoundError` handler answer 404.

The account router's account surface is `GET /accounts`, `GET /accounts/sync-status` (503 on `redis.RedisError`), `GET|PUT|PATCH /accounts/me/preferences` (stored on `auth_users.preferences` via `UserApi` with `exclude_none=True`), the CSV endpoints `POST /accounts/csv/inspect`, `POST /accounts/csv/import` and `POST /accounts/{account_id}/csv-sync`, `PATCH /accounts/{account_id}/rename`, `DELETE /accounts/{account_id}`, `GET /accounts/{account_id}/totals` and `GET /accounts/{account_id}/holdings`, the user-wide `GET /accounts/holdings` and `GET /accounts/holdings/{security_id}` paged holdings routes, and the rate-limited `POST /accounts/{account_id}/sync` which returns `{"accepted": true}` after enqueuing the broker sync.

`PositionService.get_user_holdings` aggregates holdings across every account owned by the user (grouping repository rows by `account_id` and delegating each group to `_calculate_holdings`), while `get_holdings_by_security` resolves a single security and returns an empty result when the security is unknown; both back paged account routes, and `get_account_holdings` derives `total_profit_loss` as `total_value - net_deposits` and only reports `total_profit_loss_percent` when `net_deposits` is set and non-zero.

The entity-relationship diagram's `WatchlistsSecurities` entity is not a bare join table: it stores the `added_at` and application-managed `position` columns that give each watchlist its ordering, alongside the cascading composite primary key over `watchlist_id` and `security_id`.
